definition: The 2012 neural network by Krizhevsky, Sutskever and Hinton that won the ImageNet image-recognition contest by a wide margin. It was trained on two GeForce GTX 580 gaming GPUs using CUDA.

The open-source deep-learning framework created at Meta (2016-17) and now the default in AI research. Models are written once in Python; vendor backends (CUDA first, then ROCm, TPU and others) run them.

A GPU design, introduced by NVIDIA's G80 in 2006, in which one pool of identical programmable cores handles every graphics stage. Those general-purpose cores are what CUDA exposed for non-graphics work.
Someone who has signed up to NVIDIA's developer programme. The count is cumulative and self-reported, so it measures reach rather than how many people actively write CUDA code today.
